title: Out-of-Order Window Size vs Clock Cycle Trade-off
decision: Balanced 80-entry instruction window against clock cycle time impact
rationale: Larger window improves ILP but increases cycle time; 80 entries was the optimal balance point for the target clock frequency
outcome: Achieved both high ILP and high clock frequency
weakest_point: Whether the paper explicitly frames this as a trade-off with the 80-entry number

title: Clustered Integer Execution Units
decision: Organized integer execution units into clusters to reduce wire delay
rationale: Reduces long wire delays that would otherwise limit clock frequency in a wide-issue design
outcome: Enabled 6-issue superscalar execution at high clock rates
weakest_point: Specific number of clusters and exact wire delay considerations

title: Instruction Cache Replication for Bandwidth
decision: Replicated instruction caches to provide multiple fetch ports
rationale: Increases instruction fetch bandwidth to feed the wide-issue pipeline
outcome: Reduced instruction fetch bottlenecks in the 6-issue design
weakest_point: Exact replication factor and whether alternatives were explicitly discussed

title: Wire-Delay-Driven Floorplanning Methodology
decision: Adopted wire-delay-driven floorplanning to minimize critical path delays
rationale: Prioritizes placement of critical path components to meet aggressive clock frequency targets
outcome: Achieved clock frequencies exceeding 600 MHz with balanced wire lengths
weakest_point: Specific floorplanning methodology details and whether it was presented as a decision
